summary: This paper reports a preregistered, paired confirmatory study (n=200 pairs, shared_initial_candidate semantics) that tested whether a multidimensional validator-metric suite predicts end-to-end agentic NetOps success better than a single verifier pass rate. Execution and analysis artifacts are archived and internally consistent. The run produced a degenerate (ceiling) outcome: every initial candidate was valid under the deterministic validator, no repairs were ever applied, and baseline and guarded success rates were both 200/200 (paired difference 0.00; McNemar p=1.0; 95% bootstrap CI [0.00,0.00]). The manuscript correctly acknowledges that the shared_initial_candidate design isolates downstream validator/repair utility and that the null result reflects high initial-candidate quality and limited validator coverage for semantic intent misalignment. The experimental preregistration, execution manifest, analysis, and disclosure (including the immutable master-prompt SHA-256) are present in the evidence bundle.
critical_issues: References/bibliography appear to be recorded as DOI/arXiv identifiers in the evidence bundle. The manuscript References section must present conventional, numbered IEEE bibliographic entries (authors, title, venue, year, DOI/URL) so readers and reviewers can verify claims; bare DOI/arXiv/identifier-only entries are not sufficient when full bibliographic metadata exists.

The preregistered power analysis assumed non-degenerate baseline success rates (examples used baseline p≈0.5). The manuscript does not explicitly state that the observed baseline success rate of 1.0 violates that power assumption and therefore that the primary confirmatory test could not detect the preregistered 10 percentage-point improvement. This should be clearly and prominently disclosed in Methods/Results (not only in Limitations) as a protocol-relevant consequence of the observed data.

The Disclosure Statement is comprehensive but repeats many execution-log details that are already archived; the track requires a concise Disclosure Statement that preserves the mandatory master-prompt locator/digest pair and essential autonomy/provenance facts without duplicating raw execution logs or manifest-level bookkeeping in the manuscript body.
required_revisions: Replace any identifier-only bibliography entries with full IEEE‑style numbered references (authors, title, venue, year, publisher/DOI or stable URL). Ensure each numbered in-text citation corresponds to a complete IEEE-formatted reference and that every cited record actually supports the proximate claim.

Add an explicit, prominent statement in Methods and/or Results that the preregistered power calculation assumed baseline success rates substantially below 1.0, that the observed baseline success rate = 1.0 invalidates those power assumptions, and that this ceiling effect renders the primary confirmatory test uninformative for detecting the originally planned 10 percentage‑point guarded improvement. Report the consequence for interpretation (confirmatory inference limited) alongside the existing limitation discussion.

Condense the Disclosure Statement in the manuscript to a concise form that retains all mandatory items (LLM(s) and provider, adapter/orchestration, immutable master-prompt locator and SHA‑256, preregistration identifier and confirmation that preregistration preceded execution, human-autonomy boundary summary, and sampling/ shared_initial_candidate semantics). Remove or relocate detailed execution-log-level content (paths, per-file hashes, repeated manifest statistics) from the Disclosure Statement into the archived artifact bundle and reference those artifacts from the Disclosure Statement.
optional_revisions: Add a brief, explicit pointer (one sentence) to the archived evidence-to-claim table and nearest-work comparison matrix and indicate their archive paths/manifest entries so reviewers can directly consult them (do not paste full logs into the manuscript).

In Discussion, expand a short prescriptive paragraph that outlines a minimal follow-up preregistered fault-injection design (which fault classes to inject, how many injected-faulted pairs, and how multi-sample stochastic generation would be integrated) to show concretely how the next confirmatory run would avoid the observed ceiling effect.

State in Methods that model_configuration.temperature is null/unset and reiterate the recorded manifest path; the manuscript already notes this, but a one-sentence reminder in Results near the sampling-accounting would improve reproducibility clarity.
